YOUR DATA, YOUR CHOICE

Privacy, in plain language.

Signed-in training records are saved to your FORM account. A device copy supports offline use. You can export or delete your progress.

Developer: Trust Idiong · Updated October 16, 2026

What this version does

  • Email-confirmed accounts and progress sync use the Django account server and PostgreSQL database when that service is connected.
  • No app advertising, analytics SDK, or payment system.
  • Local records and exported backups are not encrypted by FORM.
  • Hosting requests and optional video services have their own data practices.

Information you enter

FORM stores the preferences and records you choose to enter: training goals, selected gender, motivation, focus areas, optional birth year, desired feelings and rewards, exercise location, self-reported walking comfort and flexibility, experience level, age group, schedule, equipment, program dates, safety screening answers, exercise restrictions and assessments, workout history, activity logs, effort, soreness and difficulty feedback, optional weight, waist and hip measurements, favorites, custom routines, chosen program and completion records, and app settings. These can include information about your health or fitness.

Adult users can optionally record waist and hip measurements in centimetres, with dates, independently of body weight. Local history and trends reflect those entries; FORM does not create an appearance score or prescribe an ideal waist-to-hip ratio. These measurements remain part of your local records and any backup you explicitly export.

If you enable energy estimates, FORM also stores the age, body mass and effort choice you supply, and retains a snapshot of the estimate and its inputs in that session's history. This feature is optional and restricted to adults aged 19–59. It produces a rough gross-session estimate that includes rest, not a device measurement or weight-loss prediction.

Reminder settings include selected weekdays, time and the last reminder occurrence shown, to avoid repeating it. A voice preference records whether you have enabled spoken exercise cues.

We use these records within the app to personalize general fitness guidance, save and report progress, and recover an interrupted session. When signed in, FORM sends your chosen profile and training records to its account server for storage and sync. Guest records remain local until you choose to import them into an account.

Your account and email confirmation

FORM uses Django accounts and PostgreSQL storage. Signup records your email address, display name, password hash, and agreement to progress storage and owner monitoring. Signup and each new login send a short-lived email confirmation link. Access is granted only after that link is confirmed. Confirmation links expire after 15 minutes, work once, and can be resent subject to limits. The server stores a hash of the confirmation token rather than its original value.

Your existing signed-in session can stay open while you use the app; an offline device copy supports workouts between connections. Password reset uses a separate emailed link. Mailgun receives your email address and the transactional message needed to deliver these links. Authentication messages do not subscribe you to marketing campaigns. Passwords, session cookies and confirmation tokens are not included in training backups or deliberately stored in browser localStorage.

Production session cookies are HttpOnly and Secure. The app and API should run on the same HTTPS address. Rate limits help restrict repeated account and email requests. Authentication email requires the owner to configure Mailgun with a verified sender; the app reports delivery/setup failures without pretending you signed in.

Progress sync and owner monitoring

Signed-in progress is stored in your account on the Django server and PostgreSQL database, with a local device copy for offline use. When you reconnect, the app attempts to sync changes. If device copies conflict, it keeps the copies for you to review rather than silently replacing your progress.

The owner dashboard shows registered accounts, email and display name, registration and recent activity dates, workout counts and minutes, training goals and plan dates, and selected activity history. These entries are user-generated progress, not independently verified exercise measurements. The dashboard excludes your optional body measurements, weigh-ins, birth year, gender, sensitive movement choices, free-text assessment notes, and estimate inputs. Pelvic practice preferences remain private. Completed pelvic practice contributes actual activity counts and minutes and appears to the owner as a generic Private wellness session, without pelvic routine details. Current-day symptom answers stay only in the open practice screen and are not saved or synced.

Your full private profile remains in your account snapshot so it can sync to your own devices. Hosting/database administrators have operational access to the database. This service does not claim end-to-end encryption. The previous guest profile is separate and transfers to an account only when you choose to import or restore it.

Signing out keeps the device's account copy until you delete it or clear browser storage. Delete account verifies your password and deletes the server account and its progress, plus its data on this device. Other devices, exported files, calendars and retained hosting backups are not automatically erased. Use the account and progress deletion controls in Profile.

Where records live

Unfinished setup answers are saved as a local draft until you complete setup or delete local records. Records are stored in the browser's localStorage for the website address where you use the app. Cached app files support offline use after the app finishes caching. Records remain until you delete them or your browser clears or evicts site storage; private browsing may keep them only temporarily.

FORM does not add encryption or an app password to local records. Someone with access to your device or browser may be able to read them. Use your device's own security settings and avoid entering information you do not want stored here.

Another browser, device, or hosting address has its own storage. An Android launcher using a Trusted Web Activity uses the supporting browser's website storage; removing the launcher alone may leave that data in the browser.

Backups, calendar exports and restoring

Export backup creates a plain JSON file only when you request it. The file can contain your saved profile, health-related training entries, favorites, routines, program and settings. FORM does not automatically upload it. You choose where to save or share it and are responsible for protecting copies.

Restore backup reads the file you select locally in your browser. Download a backup before changing browsers or clearing site storage if you want to keep your records.

If you choose Add to phone calendar, FORM creates a calendar file with your selected training weekdays and time, plan or program dates, session duration, optional profile name and reminder alarms. Importing this file into a calendar is your choice; that calendar controls alerts, storage, sharing and any sync to its own cloud provider. The file is not encrypted by FORM and does not contain your safety answers, measurements or workout history.

Deleting your data

Use the data controls in Profile or Reports. When signed in, deleting training data first removes its account copy; reconnect before confirming deletion. It then removes goals, progress, routines, favorites, program, settings and interrupted workout from this browser. Deleting an account additionally removes server identity after verifying your current password. Cached app files stay available for offline use. You can also clear the site's data in your browser settings.

Delete separately any exported backup or calendar files, imported calendar events and copies in other browsers, devices or website addresses. Turning reminders off or deleting FORM records does not remove alerts already imported into a calendar. Device-only profiles have no server account. Signed-in accounts store progress in PostgreSQL and can be deleted through the account controls. Hosting and third-party service logs follow those providers' retention rules.

Hosting and optional services

Opening the app makes HTTPS requests to its hosting provider. The GitHub Pages version is hosted by GitHub; a ChatGPT Sites version may also be available. These providers can process request information such as IP address, browser details, timestamps and requested URLs under their own policies. Device-only records stay in your browser. Signed-in progress syncs to the Django service hosted on Render and its PostgreSQL database. Mailgun handles confirmation and password-reset emails.

When you choose to load an exercise demonstration, FORM embeds YouTube using youtube-nocookie.com where supported, or offers a link to YouTube. Loading a video or opening that link sends request information to Google/YouTube, which may use storage and process data under its own policies. Privacy-enhanced embedding does not eliminate all third-party data processing. Your FORM profile and training logs are not added to video requests.

If you enable spoken exercise cues, the browser's speech service processes movement names, interval labels and durations. The selected device voice may work locally or use an online voice provider under that provider's policies; availability varies by device. FORM does not include your profile, safety answers, measurements or workout history in spoken cues, and does not request microphone access.

Optional browser alerts require your permission and an open app. FORM does not use server push or transmit your reminder schedule to a developer server. For closed-app reminders, you can export to your calendar as described above.

FORM uses local/system fonts and does not request font files from Google Fonts.

External websites have their own policies. See GitHub's privacy statement, OpenAI's privacy policy, and Google's privacy policy.

Audience and fitness guidance

FORM provides general fitness guidance with options for ages 16–17 and adults. Flexible goals and exercise levels do not mean every program is appropriate for every medical condition or life stage. Weight-loss targets, the Curves & glute development goal and body-measurement controls are intended only for adults. The Curves goal supports strength practice; it cannot guarantee a particular body shape or selectively remove fat from an area.

The guidance has not been clinically reviewed. FORM is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition. Consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment and to discuss exercise concerns.

Contact and changes

For app or privacy questions, contact the developer through the FORM GitHub issue tracker. Issues are public: do not post health information, exported backups, passwords, or other private details.

We will update this page if the app's data practices change, including any future accounts, cloud sync, analytics, purchases, or health integrations. The date above identifies this version.
